context:
Goal: the glued-& rebuild makes the check agree with one set of rows, not two.
Problem (goal): pull request 2015, the earlier glued-& fix, carries test rows that disagree with main's rows for the same command in five groups (14 push rows, 4 owner-judge rows, 2 rule rows, 2 merge rows, 6 more rows), and your b pick on the glued-& question does not say how far it reaches into them.
Based on (ruling): own-896-897-glued-amp-b, your b pick on the glued-& question.
Based on (read): the lane's count of red rows by group, as it relayed at 15:01 CST; triage has not re-counted.
Departs from: main refuses or asks today in each of the five groups — option b follows the old pull request's row and loosens main there; option a changes nothing on main.
Meanwhile: the lane builds only the families your b pick covers.
holds: The lane builds only the families your b pick covers; the other red rows wait until you answer.

options.gain: No refusal on main gets looser; the lane finishes without waiting.
options.how: The lane keeps main's rows and drops the old pull request's conflicting rows.
options.label: Main's rule wins every time
options.lose: Your b pick covers less than you may have meant.

options.gain: Your b pick reaches every conflicting row.
options.how: The lane changes main's rule to match each of the old pull request's rows.
options.label: The old row wins every time
options.lose: Some refusals on main become allowed or asks.

options.gain: Each group gets the answer you want.
options.how: The lane lists each group with both answers and you pick per group.
options.label: You rule each of the five groups
options.lose: The red rows stay open until you answer five picks.

title: For the glued-& rebuild, when the old pull request 2015's test rows and main's rows give opposite answers for the same command, should main's rule win (a), the old row win (b), or do you rule per group (c)?
why: The lane recommends a (its words, not yours): it loosens nothing on main.
